subject: Engineering Fundamentals
title: Foundation Failures: When the Ground Gives Way
description: One-minute skill: Foundation Failures: When the Ground Gives Way.

hook.text: The Transcona Grain Elevator in Manitoba tilted 27 degrees overnight in 1913. It sank into soft clay.

buildup.text: Builders assumed the clay beneath it was strong. They never tested it. The soil couldn't bear the load.

discovery.text: Karl Terzaghi later founded soil mechanics. He proved that water pressure in soil affects its strength.

twist.text: Engineers jacked the elevator upright and placed it on new piles driven to bedrock. It still operates today.

climax.text: Modern geotechnical surveys test soil layers before construction. Every tall building starts underground.

punchline.text: A structure is only as strong as the ground it stands on.

quiz.question: What caused the Transcona Grain Elevator to tilt dramatically?
options: An earthquake liquefied the sand beneath the foundation
The soft clay soil beneath it could not bear the weight
Flooding eroded the concrete piles supporting the base
